rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
$$IE:\ X(g)\rightarrow X^{+}(g)+e^{-},\qquad EA:\ X(g)+e^{-}\rightarrow X^{-}(g)$$
$$\text{electronegativity (Mulliken)}\approx\frac{IE+EA}{2}$$
$$\Delta EN>1.7\ \text{ionic},\quad 0.5<\Delta EN<1.7\ \text{polar covalent},\quad \Delta EN<0.5\ \text{non-polar}$$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Atomic radius increases across a period. ✅ It decreases because Z_eff rises faster than shielding.  ·  ❌ An anion is smaller than its parent atom. ✅ It is larger — added electrons increase repulsion while nuclear charge stays the same.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: H IE₁ = 1312 kJ mol⁻¹ (13.6 eV); He has the highest IE₁ (2372 kJ mol⁻¹); Cs one of the lowest (~376 kJ mol⁻¹).  ·  F is the most electronegative element (Pauling 4.0); Cs/Fr least (~0.7).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Arrange Mg²⁺, Na⁺, F⁻, O²⁻ in decreasing size. **Solution:** they are isoelectronic (10 electrons), so the smallest nuclear charge gives the largest radius → O²⁻ (Z = 8) > F⁻ (9) > Na⁺ (11) > Mg²⁺ (12).  ·  **Problem:** Which has the higher first ionisation energy, Be or B? **Solution:** Be (899 kJ mol⁻¹) > B (801 kJ mol⁻¹), since Be's 2s² is a filled subshell and its electron penetrates closer to the nucleus than B's 2p electron.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: periodic trend, periodicity: atomic radii, ionic radii, ionization energy (within Classification of Elements and Periodic Table).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Meaning of periodicity  ·  Periodicity is the recurrence of similar physical and chemical properties at regular intervals when elements are arranged in order of atomic number. Its cause is the periodic repetition of the *valence-shell electronic configuration*: trends across a period follow from increasing Z_eff, trends down a group from increasing n and increasing shielding.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Isoelectronic radii: N³⁻ > O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺.  ·  answer pattern for "Periodic trend and periodicity: atomic radii, ionic radii…": define → method → result. Structure earns the marks on 6–10 mark questions.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: state + explain the main idea of "Periodic trend and periodicity: atomic radii, ionic radii…" with one example.  ·  compare "Periodic trend" with the related idea from a neighbouring unit.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Explain every trend with Z_eff (across) and n plus shielding (down) — the mark is for the reason, not the direction.  ·  Quote the anomaly pairs Be–B, N–O, Mg–Al and P–S with reasons; they are frequently examined.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### 2. Atomic radii  ·  Radius is measured as covalent radius (half the bond length in a homonuclear molecule), metallic radius (half the distance between neighbouring metal atoms) or van der Waals radius (from non-bonded contacts — the largest).…  ·  ### 3. Ionic radii

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • Electron affinity  ·  • Electronegativity  ·  ❌ IE increases smoothly across a period. ✅ Be > B and N > O (also Mg > Al, P > S) are standard breaks from 2s² stability and 2p pairing.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Fluorine has the highest electron affinity. ✅ Chlorine does (349 vs 328 kJ mol⁻¹) because of extra repulsion in F's tiny 2p shell.  ·  ❌ Electronegativity is directly measurable. ✅ It is a derived, scale-dependent parameter (Pauling, Mulliken, Allred–Rochow).  ·  State the radius type and the electronegativity scale whenever numbers are quoted.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Arrange N³⁻, O²⁻, F⁻, Na⁺ and Mg²⁺ in order of increasing radius and justify the order.  ·  Why is the electron affinity of chlorine greater than that of fluorine?  ·  Explain the variation of metallic character across a period and down a group with examples.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: • A cation is smaller than its parent atom (Na 186 pm → Na⁺ 95 pm); an anion is larger (Cl 99 pm → Cl⁻ 181 pm) because added electrons increase repulsion while the nuclear charge is unchanged.  ·  • Down a group the ionic radius increases for the same charge (Li⁺ < Na⁺ < K⁺ < Rb⁺ < Cs⁺); across a period ions of the same charge get smaller.  ·  • **Isoelectronic series** (same number of electrons): radius decreases as nuclear charge increases, N³⁻ > O²⁻ > F⁻ > Ne > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺; for one element Fe³⁺ < Fe²⁺.
